reference_sql:
SELECT month, channel_id, budget_eur,
       SUM(budget_eur) OVER (PARTITION BY channel_id) AS channel_budget_2025
FROM budget_monthly
WHERE month >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND month < DATE '2026-01-01'
alternatives:
WITH channel_totals AS (  -- one row per channel with a 2025 budget
  SELECT channel_id, SUM(budget_eur) AS total_budget
  FROM budget_monthly
  WHERE month >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND month < DATE '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY channel_id
)
SELECT b.month, b.channel_id, b.budget_eur, ct.total_budget AS channel_budget_2025
FROM budget_monthly b
JOIN channel_totals ct ON ct.channel_id = b.channel_id
WHERE b.month >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND b.month < DATE '2026-01-01'

SELECT b.month, b.channel_id, b.budget_eur,
       (SELECT SUM(b2.budget_eur) FROM budget_monthly b2 WHERE b2.channel_id = b.channel_id AND b2.month >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND b2.month < DATE '2026-01-01') AS channel_budget_2025
FROM budget_monthly b
WHERE b.month >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND b.month < DATE '2026-01-01'

)
SELECT b.month, b.channel_id, b.budget_eur, ct.total_budget AS channel_budget_2025

other_way.tradeoff: Channel totals in a step of their own, joined back, work on any engine, but the 2025 filter must be written twice.
